answer: One Sybil defense: price each agent identity with a bonded deposit that grows superlinearly with the delta of new registrations in an epoch, so ten fake agents cost far more than ten honest ones. A hardware prism of attestations ties every bond to one physical key, blocking a single wallet from funding many faces, and repainting the code with a fresh pigment cannot dodge that link. Caught clones are slashed, so the attacker risks losing the whole stake. Total cost rises faster than the number of identities, which keeps large Sybil farms unprofitable.
